articles.title: Deutsche Bank sees 3 straight Fed hikes after hot CPI, adding a January move
articles.description: A no-pause path into March is more hawkish than markets have priced beyond December. If other banks follow, it would likely be repriced through the front end of the Treasury curve and the dollar. That keeps USD/JPY pressed toward the 160 area where Tokyo is already warning, and it adds to the headwinds for gold. For equities, a faster sequence of hikes lands at an awkward moment, with AI stocks already under pressure from the Nvidia leadership shock. Oil remains the wildcard: renewed energy-driven inflation would strengthen the case for back-to-back hikes, while a sustained easing in crude would weaken it. --- Deutsche Bank has turned UBS’s “faster tightening” risk into its base case, and the Fed debate is now about the pace after December, not whether December happens. Summary: Deutsche Bank now expects 25bp Fed hikes in December, January and March, adding a January move to its previous December and March path That would lift the federal funds target range to 4.50% to 4.75%, from 3.75% to 4% now The revision followed October CPI, which rose 0.4% m/m against a 0.3% forecast, and which the bank said showed broad-based gains Deutsche Bank won’t rule out a 50bp December hike after Waller’s comments, but it isn’t the bank’s base case UBS keeps a base case of hikes in December and March only Markets price a December quarter-point hike at more than 95%, according to CME FedWatch Deutsche Bank now expects the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at each of its next three meetings, after adding a January increase to its forecast following a hotter than expected US inflation report. The bank sees quarter-point hikes in December, January and March. That would lift the federal funds target range to 4.50% to 4.75%, from 3.75% to 4% now. Deutsche Bank had previously expected hikes in December and March, with a pause in January. The October consumer price report changed that view. Headline prices rose 0.4% on the month against forecasts of 0.3%, and the bank said the data continued to show broad-based gains. The bank also addressed the idea of a larger move. Before the data, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50 basis point hike should be considered in December if price pressures accelerated, and Deutsche Bank said his comments opened that possibility. It would not rule out a half-point increase, but said a 50 basis point move is not its base case. The revision puts Deutsche Bank at the more hawkish end of the major banks. UBS, for example, said this week it sees limited support on the rate-setting committee for a 50 basis point step. It keeps a base case of quarter-point hikes in December and March only, although it flagged the risk of more or faster tightening. The two views share a common thread: the debate has shifted from whether the Fed hikes in December to how quickly it follows through. Markets are close to fully pricing a December move. Traders put the odds of a quarter-point hike at the December 8-9 meeting above 95%, according to CME FedWatch. The path matters well beyond bonds. Three consecutive hikes would keep pressure on Treasury yields, which climbed close to 5% after the CPI release, and would support the dollar. It also raises the bar for assets that have struggled with higher rates, from gold, which has slipped back below $4,000 an ounce, to richly valued technology stocks. The next tests come from November’s labor market data and further Fed commentary before the December meeting. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Axi joins Babypips as an advertising partner through its Trusted Partner programme
articles.description: The arrangement gives Axi an opportunity to introduce its trading services to Babypips' established global audience through its advertising platform SYDNEY, Nov. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Axi, a global online FX and CFD broker, has joined Babypips as an advertising partner through its Trusted Partner programme, providing an opportunity to increase brand visibility among an established audience of forex traders and those looking to learn more about financial markets. Founded in 2005, Babypips has become an established online destination for forex education, helping millions of readers understand the foreign exchange market. Its accessible learning resources explain forex trading and the economic forces that influence currency prices and wider financial markets. Its educational offering includes the School of Pipsology, a structured, self-paced programme with free courses covering forex basics and technical analysis. Its Premium curriculum goes further into price action, macro fundamentals, intermarket analysis, global liquidity and trading plan development, with a strong emphasis on risk management. Babypips also offers market commentary, trading tools, quizzes and a community forum. Through the Trusted Partner programme, Axi will be featured as an advertising partner on Babypips, giving readers the opportunity to discover more about the broker and its trading services through designated promotional placements. The arrangement provides Axi with access to a relevant audience while allowing Babypips to maintain a distinction between advertising partnerships and its independent educational and editorial content. "Babypips has built an established presence within the forex education space, reaching an audience interested in understanding and participating in financial markets. Becoming an advertising partner through its Trusted Partner programme gives Axi an opportunity to increase our visibility among this audience and introduce more traders to our offering," said Julie Sharova, Global Head of Marketing at Axi. To support traders at every stage, the School of Pipsology has continually evolved beyond introductory forex into advanced market study. Its latest curriculum updates feature specialised modules on price action trading, macro fundamentals, global liquidity, and a practical prop firms 101 guide. Alongside these structured lessons, the platform's active community forums provide an open space for traders around the world to debate strategy, analyse market movements, and share ideas in real time. About Axi Axi is a global online FX and CFD broker, providing thousands of clients across 100+ countries with access to financial markets through intuitive trading platforms, advanced tools, and educational resources. Its product suite includes forex, CFDs, and perpetual futures, with availability varying by region and entity. About Babypips Founded in 2005, Babypips is one of the world's most trusted online resources for retail traders. The platform is best known for its flagship School of Pipsology. Beyond education, Babypips empowers market participants with MarketMilk, an intuitive visual technical analysis and screening tool, and daily market commentary authored entirely by its veteran in-house editorial team. The team covers forex, equities, commodities like gold and oil, and broader financial markets. Backed by an active global trading community, Babypips equips millions of readers each month with clear, actionable insights to navigate modern investing. For more information, visit www.babypips.com. Copyright 2026 GlobeNewswire, Inc.

articles.title: LG ELECTRONICS' PRISM AI WINS THREE HONORS AT 2026 AMEC AWARDS
articles.description: LG's AI-Powered Platform Recognized for Measuring the Real-World Impact of Communications News Summary LG Electronics' PRISM AI has won Gold in the Best Use of AI in Communication Measurement category and Silver in both the Best Use of a Measurement Framework category and the Step Change Award at the 2026 AMEC Global Communication Effectiveness Awards. The platform was recognized for its data-handling and impact measurement, which have helped expand LG's media monitoring from 53 to 200 countries and cut reporting time from about one month to one hour. A notable example of LG Group's focus on AI transformation (AX), PRISM AI has now been recognized by two major international industry awards this year, including the Best AI Tool or Product category at the 2026 IN2 SABRE Awards Asia-Pacific.SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Electronics (LG) today announced that PRISM AI, its AI-powered communications measurement platform, has won three honors at the 2026 AMEC Global Communication Effectiveness Awards. The awards are presented by AMEC, the International Association for the Measurement and Evaluation of Communication. LG_PRISM AI AMEC Award The platform earned Gold in the Best Use of AI in Communication Measurement category and Silver in both the Best Use of a Measurement Framework category and the Step Change Award, which recognizes the best improvement of a measurement journey. The accolades highlight PRISM AI's potential as a reference point for the public relations and communications industry. How the Awards Were Judged This year, the AMEC Global Communication Effectiveness Awards adopted a threshold-based judging model, under which each entry is evaluated against fixed criteria for excellence rather than against other entries. To protect the integrity of the process, judges are not permitted to use generative AI tools to support or inform their evaluations. The judging places the greatest emphasis on real-world effectiveness: how reliable the findings are, whether they were acted on, and how they shape future communications planning and strategy. These priorities are reflected in PRISM AI's approach, with its integrated measurement methodology and multilingual contextual analysis designed to address these criteria, delivering dependable measurement and insights that inform business decisions. Measuring Impact, Not Just Volume PRISM AI measures the impact of communications, not just the volume of coverage. The platform is built around three core concepts from AMEC's Barcelona Principles 3.0: outcomes over outputs, quality plus quantity, and transparency. To put these principles into practice, it uses a dual-metric system made up of the PR Score and the Communications Impact Index. Underpinning this approach is the platform's ability to handle data at scale. To track coverage across a fragmented global media landscape, PRISM AI processes large volumes of articles in real time and uses large language models to interpret coverage across languages and markets, producing more meaningful and comparable insights. Measurable Gains in Efficiency and Reliability Since its introduction, PRISM AI has improved the efficiency and reliability of LG's global communications workflows. Its AI-powered filtering removes more than 78 percent of spam and irrelevant content with over 95 percent accuracy. Media monitoring now covers 200 countries, up from 53, and tracked brands have grown from 5 to 30. The time spent on reporting has been reduced from approximately one month to one hour. Growing International Recognition As LG Group advances AI transformation (AX) across its businesses, PRISM AI has become an internationally recognized example of AI-driven data collection and analysis in a specialized professional field. The AMEC recognition follows the platform's win in the Best AI Tool or Product category at the 2026 IN2 SABRE Awards Asia-Pacific, held in Singapore this August. "Winning three AMEC Awards for PRISM AI is especially meaningful, not only because it highlights our efforts in advancing AI-powered communications measurement, but also because the recognition comes directly from the PR industry's most respected global body," said Cho Jung-bum, head of the AX Center at LG Electronics. "We will continue to refine PRISM AI's methodology while expanding its capabilities and scope, further enhancing its value as a solution for driving better business decisions." About LG Electronics, Inc. LG Electronics is a global innovator in technology and consumer electronics with a presence in almost every country and an international workforce of more than 75,000. LG's four Companies - Home Appliance Solution, Media Entertainment Solution, Vehicle Solution and Eco Solution - combined for global revenue of over KRW 89 trillion in 2025. LG is a leading manufacturer of consumer and commercial products ranging from TVs, home appliances, air solutions, monitors, automotive components and solutions, and its premium LG SIGNATURE and intelligent LG ThinQ brands are familiar names world over. Visit www.LG.com/global/newsroom/ for the latest news.

Valeura Energy Inc.: Exploration, Development, and Production Success in Q3 2026
articles.description: SINGAPORE, Nov. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Valeura Energy Inc. (TSX:VLE, OTCQX:VLERF) ("Valeura" or the "Company") reports its unaudited financial and operating results for the three and nine month periods ended 30 September 2026. The complete quarterly reporting package for the Company, including the unaudited financial statements (the "Interim Financial Statements") and associated management's discussion and analysis ("MD&A") are being filed on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and posted the Company's website at www.valeuraenergy.com. Q3 Highlights Oil production of 2.036 million bbls, averaging 22,128 bbls/d(1); Oil sales of 2.013 million bbls; Price realisations averaged US$97.4/bbl, resulting in revenue of US$196.1 million; Adjusted EBITDAX of US$115.8 million(2) and adjusted cashflow from operations of US$93.6 million(2); Net cash of US$384.9 million(3), with no debt. Exploration discovery on Block G1/48(4) ? the Suraphi oil field; Final investment decision ("FID") on the first phase of development of the Bussabong gas field, on Block G3/65(5); and Milestone cumulative production of 100 million bbls of oil from the Jasmine/Ban Yen field on Block B5/27(6) as of 21 September 2026. Recent Achievements Early completion and installation of the new Wassana central processing platform ("CPP") on Block G10/48(6). (1) Working interest share production, before royalties. (2) Non-IFRS financial measure or non-IFRS ratio ? see "Non-IFRS Financial Measures and Ratios" section. (3) Includes restricted cash of US$15.8 million. (4) 70% operated working interest. (5) 40% non-operated working interest. (6) 100% operated interest. Dr. Sean Guest, President and CEO commented: "Across the entire spectrum including exploration, development, and production, our performance in Q3 2026 provides strong examples of how we are delivering value for our stakeholders. We are firing on all cylinders. Our exploration discovery at Suraphi creates a line of sight to a longer life for the G1/48 Block by unlocking both new and stranded oil accumulations in the vicinity. Our Wassana redevelopment project demonstrates our ability to execute high value offshore developments efficiently, underscored by our two-month acceleration of the CPP installation. Our FID of the first phase of development at the Bussabong field lays a framework for us to diversify our portfolio and to build materiality from gas development over time. All of this was delivered safely, and while recording high-margin oil production exactly in line with our plan. From a financial perspective, our Q3 performance illustrates how our portfolio is pre-disposed to turning high oil prices into a formidable stream of cash flow. As a result, by the end of Q3 our balance sheet had grown to US$385 million in cash, with no debt. This position, together with our undrawn credit facility, provides the wherewithal for us to pursue our inorganic growth ambitions in Thailand and elsewhere in the region. We are excited by the opportunity set before us and see the potential for Valeura to deliver transformational growth." Financial Update The Company's Q3 2026 financial performance reflects ongoing production operations at all four of its operated fields in the offshore Gulf of Thailand, and was influenced by continuing high realised prices during the quarter, coupled with sales volumes essentially equivalent to production volumes. Valeura's working interest share production before royalties averaged 22,128 bbls/d, resulting in a total of 2.036 million bbls produced during Q3 2026, which was approximately 4% lower than Q3 2025. Production was above the Company's expectations for the quarter, and continues to support its production guidance outlook for the full year 2026 as set out in its Revised Guidance (September 2026). Oil sales totalled 2.013 million bbls during Q3 2026, which was approximately the same as production, and therefore resulted in crude oil inventory being unchanged from the beginning of the quarter. Realised prices during Q3 2026 averaged US$97.4/bbl, a 35% increase over Q3 2025, and a reflection of higher global oil benchmark prices as a result of the conflict in the Middle East. Q3 2026 revenue was US$196.1 million, an increase of 26% over Q3 2025 revenue, primarily as a result of higher realised prices. Revenue in Q3 2026 includes crude oil receivables of US$22.6 million at 30 September 2026(2), in respect of oil sales just prior to the end of the quarter. Consequently, these particular sales are included in revenue for Q3 2026, but are not reflected in the Company's cash position as at 30 September 2026. Valeura's cost of operations in Q3 2026 was influenced by continuing high prices for refined fuel products, notably diesel, which is consumed across the Company's portfolio and comprises a material proportion of the operating budget. Operating costs for the quarter totalled US$52.7 million, equating to US$25.9/bbl of oil produced. As previously disclosed, in describing its cost of ongoing operations Valeura focuses primarily on operating costs, which is an IFRS measure. However, the Company continues to provide information on Adjusted opex, a non-IFRS measure(1), for historical comparative purposes. To derive Adjusted opex, the Company adjusts for (1) the cost of leases, relating primarily to floating infrastructure used in its operations, which totalled US$6.0 million in Q3 2026; and (2) the capitalisation of inventory, amounting in Q3 2026 to (US$1.6) million. These adjustments thereby result in Adjusted opex of US$57.1 million, or US$28.1/bbl of oil produced in Q3 2026. Management estimates that the increase in the price of diesel has resulted in an addition of approximately US$3.7/bbl to its Q3 2026 Adjusted opex versus its original plan. Valeura generated adjusted cashflow from operations(1) of US$93.6 million in Q3 2026, which was 27% higher than in Q3 2025, reflecting higher cash flow margins which were driven by higher revenue more than offsetting increases in operating costs. Valeura had no cash tax payments during Q3 2026. Following the Company's cash tax payments in Q2 2026, no further Special Remuneratory Benefit ("SRB") obligations or Petroleum Income Taxes ("PITA") cash payments are anticipated for the rest of 2026. SRB and PITA for 2026 production will be paid in May 2027. PITA accrued for Q3 2026 (relating to the Nong Yao, Wassana, and Manora fields) was fully offset by the application of tax loss carry-forwards. Valeura made cash outlays in respect of its operating expenses and capex of US$93.6 million in Q3 2026, and generated Other Income, primarily related to its overriding royalty on the Rossukon field and interest income, of US$5.0 million. As a result, the Company's performance was additive to its financial position. As at 30 September 2026, cash had increased to US$384.9 million, including restricted cash of US$15.8 million. Valeura's adjusted net working capital(1) increased to US$366.5 million as at 30 September 2026, an increase of 40% from 31 December 2025. (1) Non-IFRS financial measure or non-IFRS ratio - see "Non-IFRS Financial Measures and Ratios" section. (2) Excludes Value Added Tax. Operations Update During Q3 2026, Valeura had ongoing production operations at all four of its operated Gulf of Thailand fields. One drilling rig was on contract during the quarter, until demobilisation from its final Valeura drilling operation on 18 September 2026. Jasmine / Ban Yen Oil production before royalties from the Jasmine/Ban Yen field, in Licence B5/27 (100% operated interest) averaged 8,238 bbls/d during Q3 2026. Production rates reflect the impact of a successful drilling campaign which was completed during the quarter. Valeura drilled two new wellbores from the Jasmine-C platform and two from Jasmine-D. The drilling programme included two horizontal development wells and two dual-objective deviated wells drilled for both development and appraisal targets. In addition to increasing production, the drilling programme's multi-objective wells successfully appraised several new zones, which are being studied as potential future development candidates. During Q3 2026, cumulative oil production from the Jasmine/Ban Yen field reached a milestone of 100 million bbls produced, substantially exceeding the original production estimates for the field. Nong Yao Working interest share oil production before royalties from the Nong Yao field, in Licence G11/48 (90% operated working interest) averaged 9,255 bbls/d during Q3 2026. In addition to routine production and maintenance operations in Q3 2026, Valeura advanced its project to add four additional well slots to the Nong Yao A platform and completed it in October 2026. The Company has since mobilised its new drilling rig to the Nong Yao field, where it plans to drill three wells from the new slots in Q4 2026. Wassana Oil production before royalties from the Wassana field, in Licence G10/48 (100% operated interest), averaged 2,484 bbls/d during Q3 2026. No wells were drilled on the licence in Q3 2026, and no further wells are planned to be drilled from the field's original production facility, the Mobile Offshore Production Unit ("MOPU") Ingenium. Onshore construction of the Wassana field's new CPP facility progressed ahead of schedule in Q3 2026 and was fully completed on 01 October 2026. The CPP facility's jacket structure and the CPP itself were mobilised to the field in October and safely installed on location. Hook up and commissioning of the facility has commenced and Valeura plans to begin development drilling from the CPP later in Q4 2026. In accordance with the project plan, installing the CPP will require a shutdown of production from the field's existing production facilities for approximately two months, to execute upgrades to the field's floating storage and offloading vessel. This shutdown is scheduled to begin in mid-November 2026. Manora Working interest share oil production before royalties from the Manora field, in Licence G1/48 (70% operated working interest), averaged 2,148 bbls/d during Q3 2026. During Q3 2026 Valeura drilled the Manora-9 open water exploration well, approximately 4.5 km to the northeast of the Manora-A platform. The well, along with follow-up sidetracks, identified several oil-bearing sandstone intervals within separate fault blocks, thereby constituting a new field on the licence, to be known as Suraphi. Valeura's management believes the discovery is likely to justify a satellite facility development on the block. The Company is evaluating whether to pursue a fast-track development of the Suraphi field, or to first conduct further appraisal drilling in the vicinity, with a decision anticipated by the end of 2026. Block G1/65 and G3/65 In September 2026, the Cabinet of the Government of Thailand granted executive approval for the transfer of interest from PTTEP Energy Development Company Limited ("PTTEP"), a subsidiary of PTT Exploration and Production Public Company Limited to Valeura, in connection with the Company's strategic farm-in to Blocks G1/65 and G3/65. Valeura expects to complete the administrative steps to close the transfer of 40% non-operated working interest in each of the blocks before the end of 2026. Also in September 2026, Valeura and PTTEP took a final investment decision to proceed with an initial gas development at the Bussabong gas field on Block G3/65. The project will be Valeura's first organic gas development in its Thailand portfolio and entails two gas wellhead platforms tied in to nearby processing infrastructure. Valeura anticipates first production from the Bussabong field at approximately year-end 2028. In addition, Valeura and PTTEP are continuing to plan the next phases of appraisal and exploration on several focus areas in both Block G1/65 and G3/65, guided by 3D seismic data, which was acquired in 2025. T?rkiye On the West Thrace Production Leases and the West Thrace Exploration Licence, Transatlantic has satisfied the earning requirements entitling it to a 50% undivided working interest, but in Q3 2026, notified Valeura of its intent to relinquish its earning rights. Accordingly, Valeura's interest remains 63% in these blocks and 100% in the Banarli Licence. The Company intends to seek a new farm-in partner to pursue the next phases of exploration and appraisal on its tight gas play in T?rkiye. Valeura's management remains primarily focused on executing to add value through its growth-oriented strategy in the Asia-Pacific region, but continues to see the T?rkiye tight gas play as a potentially significant source of value in the longer term. Guidance Full year 2026 production is expected to be above the guidance mid-point despite a planned shutdown of the Wassana field now planned to begin in November 2026 rather than in 2027, in accordance with the accelerated redevelopment work plan. Operating Costs and Adjusted opex continue to be affected by higher than anticipated oil prices and the flow through effect to the cost of diesel fuel. Prices have remained at elevated levels throughout both Q2 and Q3, and are continuing into Q4 2026. As a result, the Company now anticipates its full year Adjusted opex being just above the top end of its Revised Guidance (September 2026) range. Accordingly, Valeura is adjusting its guidance on Adjusted opex as indicated in the Revised Guidance (November 2026) figures below. All capital projects associated with Valeura's original 2026 work programme, and those added by way of its Revised Guidance, as announced in May and September 2026, remain on budget. Non-IFRS Financial Measures and Ratios Adjusted EBITDAX: is a non-IFRS financial measure which does not have a standardised meaning prescribed by IFRS Accounting Standards. This non-IFRS financial measure is included because management uses the information to analyse the financial performance of the Company. Adjusted EBITDAX is a non-IFRS and non-standardised variant of EBITDAX, adjusted to remove non-cash items as well as certain non-recurring costs including severance payments and other one-off items in relation to the Company's recent acquisitions. Adjusted EBITDAX is calculated by adjusting profit for the period before other items as reported under IFRS Accounting Standards to exclude the effects of other income, exploration, SRB, finance income and expense, depletion, depreciation & amortisation ("DD&A"), other costs, and certain non-cash items (such as impairments, foreign exchange, unrealised risk management contracts, reassessment of contingent consideration and gains or losses arising from the disposal of capital assets). This non-IFRS financial measure and ratio are included because management uses the information to analyse cash generation and financial performance of the Company. Operating cost represents the operating cash expenses incurred by the Company during the period including the leases that are associated with operations, such as bareboat contracts for key operating equipment, such as FSOs, floating production, storage, and offloading vessels ("FPSO"), MOPUs, and warehouses. Adjusted opex is calculated by effectively adjusting non-cash items from the operating cost and adding lease costs. Adjusted opex is divided by production in the period to arrive at adjusted opex per barrel. Adjusted opex, as opposed to operating expenses, excludes the impacts of non-recurring, non-cash items such as prior period adjustments, and adds back lease costs in relation to FSOs, FPSOs, MOPU, and other facilities. articles.title: Cricket-Cricket Australia boss Boon backs Cummins' leadership amid 'Sandpapergate' row
articles.description: MELBOURNE, Nov 12 (Reuters) - Cricket Australia chairman David Boon has backed test captain Pat Cummins and said his job is not under threat over the allegations in Usman Khawaja's book about his role in the 2018 ball-tampering affair.
